reports.text: Pure-tone air and bone conduction, both ears. Otoscopy clear. Thresholds within normal limits 250 Hz through 2 kHz bilaterally. Notch at 4 kHz: 45 dB HL right, 55 dB HL left, with partial recovery at 8 kHz. Air-bone gap absent. Tympanometry type A both ears. Word recognition good both ears at comfortable level.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss with a 4 kHz notch, left slightly worse than right, consistent with noise exposure.

documents.title: Occupational Medicine Consultation: hearing
documents.author: occupational medicine
documents.body:
OCCUPATIONAL MEDICINE CLINIC
Date of service: 02/09/2022
Re: Craig Abbott, DOB 08/09/1973
Referred by: employer hearing conservation program after a shift on his annual audiogram

Mr. Abbott is a 48-year-old battery recycling technician, about 25 years in plant work, who has noticed hearing getting worse over the past several months, mostly trouble following conversation on the floor and in restaurants. No otalgia, no drainage, no dizziness or spinning. No tinnitus complaints today.
History: hypertension and gout. Meds: lisinopril, allopurinol 300 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father hypertension, paternal uncle gout, mother hypothyroidism.

Exam: vital signs normal. Ear canals clear. Tympanic membranes intact on both sides, pearly, no fluid or redness. Weber goes to the right. Rinne positive bilaterally, air conduction better than bone.
Audiogram today (attached): high-frequency sensorineural loss both ears with a notch at 4 kHz, left a little worse.

Assessment: Noise-induced hearing loss, bilateral, work-related.
Plan: Fitted for foam plugs plus earmuffs for loud areas. Repeat audiogram yearly through the employer program. Not at a level needing amplification at present.

Occupational Medicine Physician
cc: primary care

documents.title: Hearing test at work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the plant sent me to their occupational doctor for my hearing. He said it's from noise and gave me double protection. Just wanted you to have it. Should I be doing anything else?

documents.title: RE: Hearing test at work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks Craig, we got their letter. I agree with the plan: wear the plugs and muffs together on the floor every time, and keep doing the yearly hearing test. Nothing else needed right now. If it starts affecting you at home, we can talk about a formal hearing aid evaluation.

documents.title: Occupational Medicine Visit: weakness and abdominal pain
documents.author: occupational medicine
documents.body:
OCCUPATIONAL MEDICINE CLINIC
Date of service: 08/10/2022, with addendum 08/12/2022
Re: Craig Abbott, DOB 08/09/1973

Seen previously here in February for work-related hearing loss. Now 49, he comes back with roughly half a year of slowly increasing weakness in both hands and both feet, tiredness through the whole shift, and crampy belly pain. In the last few weeks he has also become constipated, and store-bought laxatives have done nothing.
He works the battery breaking and smelting side of the recycling plant.
PMH: hypertension, gout, noise-induced hearing loss. Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, allopurinol 300 mg daily. NKDA.
Family history unchanged from February.

Exam: BP 145/90. Mildly pale conjunctivae. Abdomen soft. Light touch and pinprick reduced in both hands to the wrists and both feet to above the ankles. Strength mildly reduced in grip.

Labs today: Hgb 10.2, MCV 74, creatinine 1.8, BUN 29, uric acid 8.5. Smear shows basophilic stippling.
Addendum 8/12: blood lead 72 mcg/dL.

Assessment: Symptomatic occupational lead poisoning with anemia, peripheral neuropathy, abdominal symptoms and reduced kidney function.
Plan:
1. Medical removal from all lead-exposed tasks effective now; employer notified per standard.
2. Oral succimer 10 mg/kg (900 mg) three times daily for 5 days, then twice daily for 14 days. Started 8/12.
3. Blood lead and CBC after the course and then at intervals per surveillance.
4. Please follow blood pressure, kidney function and gout.

Occupational Medicine Physician
cc: primary care

documents.title: Call re: lead level
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt after reviewing the occupational medicine letter. He's on day 5 of succimer, some nausea, taking it with food. Off the lead side at work since last week, doing paperwork and inventory. Still tired, belly crampy. Kidney number up to 1.8 from 1.1 last fall; told him that's part of the lead effect and we will watch it. Visit booked mid-September. Advised to avoid NSAIDs and keep up fluids.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after lead poisoning diagnosed by occ med in August.
Finished the 19-day succimer course last week. Mild nausea only. Still fatigued, hands and feet still tingly and weak, belly cramps on and off, bowels slow. No change yet, he says.
Work: still on non-lead duties, no exposure.
Meds: lisinopril 10, allopurinol 300. Succimer complete. NKDA.

Exam: BP above goal today, recheck similar. Pale. Abdomen soft, mildly tender diffusely, no guarding. Reduced light touch in glove-stocking pattern. Grip slightly weak, symmetric.

A/P
1. Lead poisoning, symptomatic, s/p chelation. Repeat lead level and CBC are being done by occ med; asked them to cc us. Expect slow improvement.
2. HTN, above goal. Plan to keep lisinopril 10 for now and recheck when he is feeling better.
3. Gout, quiet.
4. Flu vaccine today.
RTC 4-5 months, sooner if worse.

documents.title: Still not feeling right
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Still tired all the time and my stomach still bothers me. Hands and feet tingle on and off. Can I come in before my next visit? Is the lead still in me?

documents.title: RE: Still not feeling right
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry it's dragging on. Let's get you in on 2/9 and do bloodwork a few days before so we can go over it together, including another lead level. Front desk will send the lab order. If you get severe belly pain, vomiting or new weakness before then, call right away.

results.text: Microcytic red cells; basophilic stippling present.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
49M with HTN, gout, noise-induced hearing loss and occupational lead poisoning (occ med, Aug 2022), back to go over symptoms that are hanging on.

Subjective: Still worn out by mid-afternoon. Belly aches most days, dull and all over, and he is constipated, a BM every 3-4 days despite fiber. Hands and feet tingle on and off, and they feel weak when he grips tools or climbs stairs. No weight loss, no blood in stool, no fevers. Still off the lead side at the plant since August, no other exposures at home that he knows of (no remodeling, no firearms, no hobby casting).
Meds: allopurinol 300 daily, lisinopril 10 daily. Succimer finished 9/2022. NKDA.
FH: father HTN, paternal uncle gout, mother hypothyroidism.

Objective: vitals as charted. Looks pale. Abdomen with mild diffuse tenderness, no rebound, no guarding, no masses. Neuro: light touch decreased in both hands and both feet in a glove-and-stocking distribution; reflexes present.

Labs 2/6: Hgb 10.2, MCV 74, Cr 1.8, BUN 29, uric acid 9.5. Smear: basophilic stippling. Ferritin 140, so not iron deficiency. Blood lead 44 (down from 72, but up from what occ med expected after chelation).

A/P
1. Lead poisoning with persistent anemia, neuropathy, abdominal symptoms and reduced kidney function. Numbers unchanged in 6 months; lead level consistent with release from bone stores. Will call occ med today to share and coordinate on whether more chelation is needed. Must stay out of lead work.
2. Constipation from #1: more fluids and dietary fiber.
3. Gout: uric acid 9.5 on allopurinol 300; no flares.
4. HTN: continue lisinopril 10.
Recheck CBC, BMP, lead in 3 months.

documents.title: Call with occupational medicine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with his occupational medicine physician. Their view: rebound after a single course is expected, level is falling, no repeat chelation unless it climbs back over 50 or symptoms worsen. He stays on permanent removal for now with their surveillance draws. Agreed. Pt updated by phone; he's relieved there's no more of the capsules.

documents.title: Going back to my old job
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My supervisor asked when I can go back to the furnace side. Do you decide that or the plant doctor?

documents.title: RE: Going back to my old job
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Occupational medicine makes that call based on your lead levels, and the doctor's advice is to stay off lead work for now. The doctor already spoke with them this week.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Lead f/u.
Feels a lot better than February. Belly pain gone since about April, bowels regular again. Tingling in hands mostly gone; feet still buzz at night sometimes. Energy improving, back to short rides.
No lead work.
Exam: BP above goal. Color better. Abd soft, NT. Light touch mildly reduced over toes only; hands normal.
Labs drawn this morning, CBC and BMP back during visit: Hgb 12.1, MCV 80, Cr 1.6. Lead pending.
A/P: Lead poisoning, improving. Anemia and kidney function recovering. Continue removal. Physical in the fall with labs. HTN and gout unchanged, same meds.

documents.title: Lead level
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your lead level came back at 31, down from 44 in February. Going the right direction. Occupational medicine will keep checking it at work as well.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill requests lisinopril and allopurinol approved, 90 days. Physical scheduled 9/27.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Turned 50 in August. Here for physical.
Lead: continues to improve. Energy back to normal, back to long weekend rides this summer. Feet still a little numb at the toes some nights. No abdominal symptoms.
Hearing: wears plugs and muffs; yearly test at work stable per pt.
HTN: home readings 138-144/86-90.
Gout: no flares.
Meds lisinopril 10, allopurinol 300. NKDA. Former smoker. 2-3 drinks/wk.

Exam: BP above goal. Ears: canals clear, TMs normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT. Light touch slightly reduced at toes bilaterally, otherwise intact. No joint swelling. PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- Lead poisoning, recovering.
- HTN, continue current dose.
- Gout, continue allopurinol, uric acid today.
- Health maintenance: discussed PSA screening pros and cons, he wants it. Shingrix #1, flu, updated COVID today. Colonoscopy 2021 normal.
- CMP, CBC, lipids, uric acid, PSA.
Shingrix #2 in 2-6 months. 1 year physical, f/u 4-6 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Craig. Blood count is back to nearly normal, kidney number is 1.4 (better than last year's 1.8 but not quite back to where you were before the lead). PSA normal. Uric acid a bit high at about 8, no change for now since you've had no flares. Cholesterol fine.
